trails.title: Witness Report
trails.description: An unremarkable witness report. All rumors, whispers, and tales—every passerby keeps a few in their pockets.

content.text: Many mothers report that their children, scared and screaming, run back to them when playing in the park, only to have severe nightmares afterward. Each dream begins the same way: with a blurry image of a toy elephant.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: No. No! Célia!
She falls to her knees beside her friend's body, the blood pooling around her, as a whisper slithers into her mind, growing louder and louder.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Ugh ... My head ... hurts ...
Blood. A limp hand. The gem's brilliant glow. A familiar voice, the cold sneers ... Everything spirals into chaos.
The world spins, and darkness swallows everything.
Take a deep breath, Adèle.
Come. Take my hand.
Soft, muffled voices seep into her ears.
Time to wake up, dear.
When did the lights come on? After several slow blinks, she begins to make sense of the faces staring down at her.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Madame Bouanich?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Feeling better?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Take a breath; rest a moment. We are here with you now.
Seeing another figure beside them, Adèle instinctively leaps up to put Beryl behind her.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Stay away from him, Madame Bouanich! He's the one behind all this!

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Célia told me everything! She saw you turn Vincent into a monster!

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Oh, my dear girl. When we get you back to the surface, we must get you some immediate mental care.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: You've been pacing around in circles, talking to yourself, laughing, and crying for who knows what reason. And now, just as I thought Madame Bouanich had managed to calm you down, you start spouting this nonsen—

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Enough with your lies! You can't fool me!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: If you know what's good for you, you'll confess all your evil plots and come with me to the police.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Wait. Isn't that ...?
She's ready to strike, but something in her periphery catches her eye.
A small arrow mark carved into the stone beside her.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: That mark. It's the one I made earlier.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: It ... It's exactly how I made it.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: But I followed Célia; we went so far. How could I be back where I started?

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Aren't you listening? All you've done is pace in circles and mutter to yourself! And now this rubbish about Célia.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: For pity's sake, girl, look around! She's not here! Ask Madame Bouanich if you must!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: B-But I saw her with my own eyes. Félicienne stabbed her!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: It was real. It was true! She was dying in my arms. Her blood was on my face, my hands.
She holds out her hands, the very ones she used to lift the bloodied body of her dearest friend.
But there's nothing there. No stains of red, nothing but old calluses.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: How could this be?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Th-This must be another one of his deceptions. You have to believe me!
She grabs Madame Bouanich desperately, as if she were the only thing keeping her afloat.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Can't you use your divination to see the truth? Please, madame!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: You have to help Célia. She's dying somewhere.
Her voice trails off.
Adèle realizes that Beryl's answer isn't what she wants to hear.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: It seems this curse still shadows over you. What you saw were simply illusions.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Rest assured. I will do what I can to help you through this.
Beryl reaches toward her, but Adèle steps back.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Illusions? So, even you think I ...?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: But there's no mistaking it! I saw Célia and Félicienne and the diamond!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Félicienne has it. Célia told me it has to be destroyed, or else ... or else ...
The spinning returns, whispers swelling in her mind again, until she hears Beryl's puzzled tone.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: The diamond?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: You mean the one strung around your neck?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Huh?
Following Beryl's gaze, Adèle lowers her head. There, on her chest, glimmers that same brilliant blue jewel.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I-Impossible. Félicienne took it from me.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: B-But how can it be here again?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: No! This is absurd!
Confusion and shock, under the weight of her fractured mind, ignite into searing rage.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Célia was right! This wicked imitation must be destroyed!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: It must be destroyed now! Come, Feufeu!
She calls to the little dragon on her shoulder, its little flame gathering to burst into a torrent—
A blaze capable of destroying that false stone.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Huh?
But the fire never comes.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: What's wrong, Feufeu? Destroy the diamond!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Feufeu?
She feels the lack of weight before she sees it. Her beloved little companion has become the latest to disappear.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: What's going on?
But Feufeu is more than just a pet. It shares her mind and soul. It could never vanish like Célia did.
Her mind goes blank again, dizziness swelling in waves.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: This is all too strange.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Wh-What was I doing again?
Her head pounds. All sound vanishes except her own panicked breathing.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Ah, right, the diamond that Célia gave to me.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: What she said was real. I have to destroy it.
Resolve flickers to the surface, only to be dragged down by the tide of hesitation.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: But this isn't any ordinary diamond; it's the miraculous French Blue.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Do I really have the right to destroy a national treasure?
Inhale, exhale. Even that simple act stretches her mental state.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Who was it who asked me to destroy it anyway? Oh, it must've been Célia!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: But Célia ... She gave the diamond to me! Ah! It's mine!
At last, a sharp voice cuts through the noise clouding her head.
Her breathing steadies, the stabbing pain recedes.
She stops. A drowsy calm spreads through her. Every worry, every doubt slips away into a warm abyss.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Please, miss. You seem to have been through a lot. You need some rest.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Perhaps some fresh air might ease your symptoms. Come, I'll lead the way back to the surface.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: My colleagues and I have a reservation at a restaurant nearby; please, join us for dinner.
A firm hand falls on her shoulder, and at last she finds herself unable to resist it.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I think you're right, Professor.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I need some fresh air.
Adèle hears herself agreeing softly—meekly. The necklace, heavy with its vivid blue diamond, hangs against her skin—tangible, real.
As if it had always been there.
